targetText: characteristic feature of the period under review is the final partitioning of the globe
summary: By the early 20th century, all territories on Earth were claimed by imperial powers, meaning any future expansion required taking land away from other powers by force.
context: Once the entire world is colonialized, peaceful expansion becomes impossible. Future shifts in power can only occur through imperialist wars of re-division.

targetText: Finance capital is such a great, such a decisive, you might say, force in all economic and in all international relations
summary: Financial capital dominates both national economies and foreign policy, making debt and financial control more powerful than formal political borders.
context: Lenin points out that even non-colonized or semi-colonial countries (like Argentina or Portugal in his time) become economically subservient to foreign finance capital.

targetText: The non-economic superstructure which grows up on the basis of finance capital
summary: State governments, military forces, media outlets, and diplomatic institutions are shaped by financial monopolies to protect their economic interests.
context: The political superstructure (governments, courts, militaries) operates to guarantee foreign loan repayments, protect corporate investments abroad, and secure strategic resources.
